name: The first rubber tree of Thailand, Kantang

location.address: Trangkhaphum Road (ถนนตรังคภูมิ), roadside before the town of Kantang, Trang

verified_sources: Ministry of Culture Rukkha Moradok khong Phaendin 2017 list, register id 2017-58 (data/registers/thailand-rukkha.json, CC BY)

https://www.thaiholidayguide.com/attraction/the-first-rubber-tree-in-thailand/ (roadside marker and plaques in Kantang, free entry, planted 1899 by the governor Khaw Sim Bee; notes the tree has been cut and regrown more than once)

official_register.name: Ministry of Culture, Department of Cultural Promotion: Rukkha Moradok khong Phaendin (heritage trees of the land), 2017, no. 58

access: Free, open roadside memorial with plaques, no fee or gate (a tourist listing says open 24 hours). Cared for by Kantang municipality per the register.
transport: Roadside at the entrance to Kantang town; a tourist guide says a short walk from Kantang railway station (not verified). Kantang is about 25 km south-west of Trang city (distance from general knowledge, not a source; train/songthaew not verified).
verify_notes: Register 2017-58: 116 years, girth 2 m, height 20 m, in the care of Kantang municipality; history text says Phraya Ratsadanupradit Mahison Phakdi wanted rubber from Malaya but the British refused; Phra Sathonsathanphitak brought seedlings back from Indonesia and planted the first one at his residence in Kantang in B.E. 2444 (1901); the governor then trained officials and spread planting, hence honoured as father of Thai rubber. Sources disagree: the register says seedlings from Indonesia in 1901, the tourist guide says British Malaya in 1899 planted by the governor. Say both, flag. CAUTION on alive and original: the tourist guide reports visitors noting the trunk has been cut and regrown more than once, so it may be a regrown original or successor at the historic spot; the page should present it as the planting site and not claim a 125 year old trunk. Girth 2 m, 20 m height are register values (2017). A living rubber tree stands there now: OSM node (created recently, id in the 13.27 billion range, so 2025) names it. Pin: OSM tree node and register coordinate agree within about 5 m. Hevea trees are normally tapped for latex and live about 30 years in plantations, so a 2 m girth trunk of 116 years is unlikely to be a single unbroken stem, another reason to hedge. No Commons photo checked.
story:
Thailand's first rubber tree, by the official account, was planted at the edge of Kantang, and a rubber tree still grows on the spot.

The Ministry of Culture listed it in 2017 as a heritage tree of the land and tells the story this way. Phraya Ratsadanupradit, the governor of Trang, wanted rubber seedlings from Malaya and was refused. An official, Phra Sathonsathanphitak, brought them back from Indonesia instead and planted the first at his residence in Kantang in 1901. The governor then trained officials and spread planting through the province, and he is remembered as the father of Thai rubber. A tourist guide tells it differently, with seedlings from Malaya planted in 1899 by the governor himself. Both accounts put the first tree here.

What you find now is a roadside memorial with plaques beside a living rubber tree, about 20 metres tall and two metres round by the register's 2017 measure. Visitors have reported that the trunk has been cut back and regrown more than once, so treat this as the place where it began rather than a trunk from 1901. We give it no age.

It stands on Trangkhaphum Road at the entrance to Kantang, south-west of the city of Trang, free to visit at any hour.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the roadside memorial with plaques beside the tree on Trangkhaphum Road, at the entrance to Kantang town.

name: Rain tree of Wat Thammawut Saranaram, Nuea Khlong
age_estimate: more than about 200 years, by the abbot's account

location.address: Wat Thammawut Saranaram (formerly Wat Bo Phlo), Ban Khlong Siat, Pakasai, Nuea Khlong, Krabi

story:
Nobody planted this rain tree. The abbot of Wat Thammawut Saranaram told Thailand's Ministry of Culture that it came up by itself and was already growing before the temple was founded, so nobody knows the year.

The temple was once called Wat Bo Phlo, and the abbot counts it as the second temple in Krabi province. Reasoning from that history, the register puts the tree at more than about 200 years. It listed the tree in 2018 as a heritage tree of the land and measured a trunk 8.12 metres round and about 25 metres tall. The abbot's account adds that today's crown grew out again from the original trunk.

A rain tree, Samanea saman, is a shade tree from tropical America with a broad, low dome of a crown.

We have not yet confirmed exactly where it stands. The temple is at Ban Khlong Siat in Pakasai subdistrict, Nuea Khlong, and the pin on our map is the register's own point, which may lie some way off. Ask for Wat Thammawut Saranaram, or its old name, Wat Bo Phlo. It is a working temple, so dress as you would for any wat. If you find the tree, send us a photograph from beside it, so the next visitor can walk straight there.

name: Fig tunnel of Khlong Sang Ne, Takua Pa
age_estimate: more than 100 years (PPTV 2023); about 200 by the register

location.address: Khlong Sang Ne, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang Nga (community boat trips)

story:
On Khlong Sang Ne, a short canal near Takua Pa, old figs lean in from both banks and meet overhead, so the boats pass through a green tunnel with roots hanging down into the water. People here call it the Little Amazon.

Thailand's Ministry of Culture listed the canal's fig as a heritage tree of the land in 2017. Its record, written from what the Khlong Sang Ne community told it, describes a tunnel of blunt-leaved weeping figs more than 200 years old, the largest over two metres round and more than 20 metres tall, among waterside trees whose roots lock together along both banks. Fresh and salt water mix here, and the register names hornbills and snakes among the wildlife. A 2023 report by the broadcaster PPTV put the tunnel at more than 100 years, so read the age as a range.

The trips are run by the community in paddle boats, with no motors, and take about an hour and a half. PPTV advises booking ahead so the trip can be timed to the tide. Takua Pa lies north of Khao Lak, a little over an hour's drive from Phuket.

Our pin is the register's point beside the canal, and we have not yet confirmed where the boats leave from, so ask the community tourism group when you book.

Location not verified: the pin is the register's point beside the canal, about 300 m from the Khlong Sang Ne access road, not a confirmed boat launch.
transport: Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa district, Phang Nga, north of Khao Lak; a little over an hour's drive from Phuket (PPTV). Public transport not verified.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the tunnel of figs arching over Khlong Sang Ne, their roots hanging into the water, on the paddle-boat route at Bang Nai Si.
